key_insight: Variantscape combines NLP and large language models to extract variant–treatment–cancer associations from oncology abstracts at scale.
clinical_relevance: The tool may support evidence discovery and molecular tumour board preparation, but extracted associations do not establish treatment benefit or clinical actionability.
method: Screen biomedical abstracts for gene mentions.
Extract and standardise variants, cancer types, and therapies using NLP and LLMs.
Use LLMs to verify associations against abstract text and build a literature-derived graph.
evidence_signal: Of 886,195 gene-containing abstracts, 37,895 (4.3%) mentioned all three entity types; LLM verification identified at least one association in 35,224 papers, yielding 44,644 verified graph edges.
watch_item: The abstract reports LLM-based verification but no independent expert-validation accuracy, so extraction reliability remains uncertain.
paper_title: Variantscape: Retrospective Study of Large Language Model-Based Extraction of Variant-Treatment-Cancer Associations from Published Oncology Abstracts
